$comment: ACP harnesses, keyed by the harness id the chat runtime uses.
Every harness drives the agent CLI the user already has, found the same way
a Superset terminal finds it: the ~/.superset/bin wrapper when it is
provisioned, else the bare name on the login shell's PATH. Nothing here is
bundled with the app, so a CLI the user upgrades is the one chat uses.
binary       the executable name; also the ~/.superset/bin wrapper name
args         argv that puts that CLI into ACP mode
minVersion   lowest version these args are known to work with
adapter      npm package that translates ACP for a CLI that cannot speak it
executableEnv  env var that adapter reads to find the CLI
upgrade      command shown to a reader whose CLI is missing or too old
note         why minVersion is what it is; keep it current when you edit
Raising or lowering minVersion is a one-line edit here. Lowering one needs
evidence: run the handshake against that version first, because an agent
below the floor fails at session/new rather than at launch.

codex-acp.note: Conservative: the adapter drives `codex app-server`, and the release that introduced it is not pinned. Set to the latest release at authoring time; lower it once a older version is verified.

gemini-acp.note: Conservative. `--acp` replaced `--experimental-acp`, and the rename release is not pinned beyond being above 0.20.0, which defined only the experimental spelling. Sending `--acp` to a CLI that predates it prints usage and exits 0, which looks like a crash, so the floor errs high.
